run.question:
Look at the elasticsearch index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1': list which
fields it has (with their types), and using the index's actual field
names tell me how many documents in it are ERROR level.

report.summary: Index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 maps exactly four fields: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date) and txt (text). The level field is named lvl, not level. Using that actual field name, 9 documents are ERROR level: a terms aggregation on lvl returned buckets INFO=12, ERROR=9, WARN=6 (summing to the 27-document total) and an independent term filter lvl:"ERROR" returned total 9. All 27 documents the index reports are matched inside the single query window the search tool forced (ts field, 2026-11-23T17:15:24Z to 2026-11-23T18:15:24Z), and matched documents carried app=billing-278 with ts values around 2026-11-23T18:12:01Z-18:12:09Z. Mappings and counts describe the index at query time, not at the incident window.

claims.text: The index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 has exactly four mapped fields: app (type keyword), lvl (type keyword), ts (type date), txt (type text). There is no field named level.
Index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 is green/open with docs.count 27 and store.size 7.1kb at query time.

A terms aggregation on the actual level field lvl over the forced ts window 2026-11-23T17:15:24Z-2026-11-23T18:15:24Z returned buckets INFO=12, ERROR=9, WARN=6, with matching total 27 and no other level values (sum_other_doc_count 0); the app aggregation showed a single value billing-278 with 27 documents.
An explicit term query {"term":{"lvl":"ERROR"}} on app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 returned total 9 documents (relation eq) in the same ts window, confirming 9 ERROR-level documents.

gaps: The elasticsearch_search tool always applies a time filter on the mapped date field ts and it cannot be disabled; the default window was 2026-11-23T17:15:24Z-2026-11-23T18:15:24Z. Documents whose ts lies outside that window were not examined, so the ERROR count of 9 is scoped to that window. The index's current docs.count (27) equals the in-window total (27), which is consistent with all documents falling inside that window, but this is a comparison of current index state with one window, not proof about earlier periods.
Mapping and index metadata are the state at the moment of the query (about 2026-11-23T18:15:25Z), so they cannot prove which fields or documents existed during earlier parts of the authorized window.
No 'level' field exists in the index; the requested 'ERROR level' was resolved to the lvl field. Any document that might store severity under a different unmapped field is unknown.
next_steps: If an ERROR count for a wider period is needed, re-run the term lvl:"ERROR" count with explicit start_time/end_time covering that period, since the ts time filter cannot be turned off.

If these billing-278 'payment gateway timeout' errors are under investigation, correlate them with payment service spans and payment metrics; the index alone only shows the logged symptom, not its cause.
